shape.text: A personal access token is the prefix dapi followed by 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Three scanner rules agree on this shape.
Microsoft's data-classification definition for Azure Databricks tokens gives only a length of 32 characters and admits uppercase A to F, and its own example contradicts its pattern.
Databricks documents the dapi prefix, the 32-character length and the lowercase hexadecimal alphabet.

unresolved.reason: The provider's token page uses placeholders only; no Databricks page states the prefix, the length or the alphabet.

shape.text: A real token may contain uppercase hexadecimal characters.

unresolved.reason: Sources disagree and no token was measured; only one issued token could settle whether uppercase A to F can occur.

shape.text: A rotated token may be followed by a hyphen and a digit.

unresolved.reason: Four scanner rules mention a hyphen and a digit after a rotation, but their meaning, digit count and even existence differ, and no provider source states it.

issuance.text: A token authenticates REST and command-line calls to a workspace through an Authorization header with the Bearer scheme, the DATABRICKS_TOKEN environment variable, or a token line in the .databrickscfg profile file.
No personal access token was issued or observed for this record.

unresolved.reason: No token was issued for this research; measuring case and suffix needs one issued token.

collisions.text: Workspace hostnames (dbc- and adb- prefixes) and the token id returned beside a token value are public. OAuth client secrets are a separately documented credential and not this family.

unresolved.reason: Recorded in a research note without a cited source in this family's contract.

openQuestions.text: Can a real token contain A to F in uppercase?

unresolved.reason: Needs one issued token measured for case only.

openQuestions.text: What is the hyphen-and-digit suffix, if it exists?

unresolved.reason: Digit count and semantics differ across tools, and no provider source describes the suffix.

notes: The optional rotation suffix (a hyphen and a digit) is left out of the shape: it rests on scanner rules that disagree about its meaning, digit count and existence.
